title: Gut microbiota-derived extracellular vesicles of patients with Parkinson's disease
projectDescription: Fecal samples were collected from 20 patients with Parkinson’s disease and 19 healthy controls at Oulu University Hospital, Oulu, Finland. Gut microbiota -derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) were isolated from fecal samples and EV-proteins were analyzed with LC-ESI-MS/MS.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Gut microbiota-derived EVs were isolated from filtrated and concentrated fecal sample suspensions using size exclusion chromatography and density gradient ultracentrifugation. EV-proteins were isolated using methanol precipitation. EV-proteins were transferred to a separating gel using SDS-PAGE. Gel bands were cut and dried with ethanol.   Dried gel-incorporated EV-protein samples were analyzed at Turku Bioscience proteomics facility (Turku, Finland). Gels were rehydrated and washed with water. Proteins were reduced with mM 1,4-dithiotreitol for 30 minutes following dehydration of gels with 100% acetonitrile (ACN). Gels were alkylated with 55mM iodoacetamide for 20 min in dark at RT and washed twice with 100 mM ammonium bicarbonate. Gels were dehydrated with ACN and dried with vacuum centrifugation for 5 minutes. Gels were digested with 0.02 µg/µl trypsin for 20 minutes and covered with 10 % ammonium bicarbonate solution overnight at 37 °C. Peptide extraction was done by treating Gels with 100% ACN. Gels were vortexed and incubated for 15 minutes at 37 °C. Supernatant was collected.  Peptide extraction was repeated with 50 % ACN / 5 % formic acid solution. Supernatant was dried with vacuum centrifugation and samples were stored at -20 °C. For mass spectrometry, samples were suspended in formic acid. Liquid chromatography-electrospray ionization-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-ESI-MS/MS) analysis was done with nanoflow HPLC system (Easy-nLC1200, Thermo Fisher Scientific) and coupled with Q Exactive HF mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) equipped with a nano-electrospray ionization source. Samples were loaded on a trapping column and were separated on a 15 cm C18 column (75µm x 15 cm, ReproSil-Pur 5µm 200 Å C18-AQ, Dr. Maisch HPLC GmbH). The mobile phase included water with 0,1% formic acid (solvent A) and ACN / water (80:20 v/v) with 0,1 % formic acid (solvent B). Peptides were eluted with linear gradient (8% to 43%) of solution B for 10 min. Data was received by using Thermo Xcalibur 4.1 software (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Mass range of 300-2000 m / z was covered including high-energy collisional dissociation fragmentation of the 10 most intense peptide ions.
dataProcessingProtocol: Data analysis of the proteomic data was done using Peaks Studio software (version 10.6). Proteomic data was searched against the UniProt Swissprot and UniProt trEMBL databases (UniProt database version 2022_05). Error tolerance was adjusted to 10 ppm and 0.02 Da for parent mass and fragment mass tolerance, respectively. False discovery rate was set to 1 % for peptides and proteins. Coverage threshold of 1% was set for accepted protein identification. Negative control, analyzed together with EV-proteins, was used to exclude possible contaminants present in the EV-protein identification results.
